subject: TemplateWorks renewal: parallel benchmark, uplift capacity & rescue plan
messages:
From: Oliver Price <oliver@templateworks.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jillian Yang <jillian@templateworks.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation & quick benchmark request

Neha,

We're approaching our annual renewal and I wanted to flag where we are: the product team is concerned about token costs and occasional latency spikes during peak checkout traffic. We're also running a fast evaluation of another vendor (ZenServe) — it's a short side-by-side focused on 99th percentile latency and cost per 1M tokens.

Before templates get formal, can you share an apples-to-apples throughput/latency profile for the last quarter and any recommended guardrails for an uplift from 2 to 4 GPUs? If Redwood can give a short-term uplift path and a bridge on price for an expanded pilot, we may be able to keep momentum on the renewal rather than running a full RFP.

Attaching a brief capacity/usage snapshot. Can you propose a two-week benchmark plan we can run in parallel with ZenServe?

Thanks,
Oliver
Director of Infrastructure
TemplateWorks
[Attachment: capacity_report_q3.pdf (pdf)]
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Price <oliver@templateworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation & quick benchmark request

Oliver — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the usage snapshot. Understandable pressure on 99th pctl during flash checkout windows. High level plan below; happy to jump on a call tomorrow.

Proposed short plan (two-week parallel benchmark):
- Week 0 (prep): we provide a benchmark-setup.yaml (lightweight) and a dedicated trial key for a 2-week uplift to a 4-GPU pool.
- Week 1: run parallel tests against your traffic profile (you control sampling); we stream token-level latency metrics to a shared dashboard.
- Week 2: validation + tuning — we’ll test prefix/KV caching and an aggressive batching profile to hit target cost reductions.

Commercial offers we can put on the table to avoid a full RFP:
- A 3-month pilot amendment for uplifted capacity + a 12% pilot discount on incremental tokens during the pilot window.
- If metrics meet agreed SLOs (99th pctl latency and cost/unit thresholds), convert to a capacity uplift commit with a step-down discount schedule.

I’ve looped Ben to align on commercial language and Marcus on the tech runbook. I’ll attach the benchmark config and a short runbook in the next email.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Price <oliver@templateworks.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial options for TemplateWorks uplift pilot

Oliver — following Neha's runbook, here are pragmatic commercial terms we can offer to shorten cycle and preserve your timeline: 

1) Pilot amendment (2 weeks trial + 10 day validation)
   - Incremental capacity pricing: 20% off list for incremental tokens during pilot period.
   - If you sign the pilot amendment by Aug 5 we’ll include one-time onboarding credits equal to one week of uplift usage.

2) Renewal bridge (conditional)
   - If pilot meets SLOs we will provide a 12-month capacity tier with a committed minimum at a blended rate that is 8% below your current rate.

3) Escape clause: 30-day opt-out after pilot conversion if agreed metrics are not sustained.

Laura — we’ll need SOC2 evidence and a one-page technical attestation. Oliver, I can get the formal pilot amendment to you as a DocuSign link today if you'd like to expedite.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
